post.summary: Start a background count of the members a message or alert would reach: `audience` is "everyone" or a rule of the criteria engine with at least one condition (an empty rule is refused, so a rule builder left empty cannot reach every member), any criterion. Members who are banned, erased, unconfirmed or awaiting approval are never written to. The count runs the delivery chunk by chunk and undoes it, so nothing is sent, queued or alerted, and broadcasts.status reports how many would be reached and how many skipped (a member without `conversation.receive`, or who turned the alert off). Returns queued false when a run is under way, and a conflict while a run is stopped or failed: resume it (broadcasts.resume) or discard it (broadcasts.discard) first. Sending as another member needs admin.members over that member. Requires admin.announcements; no password. Every send comes from a count: count the recipients of the message or alert, then send what was counted.

Send the content and audience of the latest run, which must be a finished count whose `startedAt` (from broadcasts.status) is `countedAt`: a conflict otherwise, so what is sent is the count the administrator looked at and not a newer one. A private message (one conversation per member, never one conversation with many participants; the members' block lists are not read, and each member is alerted that they were added) or an alert (notification type `admin.alert`; in the alert list, pushed by default, e-mailed only if the member opted in). It runs in small chunks in the background; broadcasts.stop ends it and broadcasts.resume continues it. Returns queued false when a run is under way, and a validation error when the latest run is not a finished count. Requires admin.announcements and, for a message sent as another member, admin.members over them. Needs `actorPassword`, the acting administrator's own password: a browser session must send it, and an API key or token cannot send.

Continue the run that stopped (by broadcasts.stop or an error) from the member it stopped at, with its own content and audience. `runAt` and `kind` name the run as broadcasts.status showed it: a conflict when the stopped or failed run is another one (another administrator may have discarded it and started their own). A send needs `actorPassword` as broadcasts.send does; a count needs none. Returns queued false when a run is under way, and a validation error when the run named is no longer stopped or failed. Requires admin.announcements.

Give up the run that stopped or failed, so another can start: what a send already sent stays sent. `runAt` and `kind` name the run as broadcasts.status showed it: a conflict when the stopped or failed run is another one (another administrator may have discarded it and started their own). Needs `actorPassword` for a send, none for a count. Logged. Returns discarded false when none is stopped or failed. Requires admin.announcements.

Send the message or alert to one member at once, as a run would: the acting administrator by default, or the member `recipientId`. No password and no audience. `delivered` is false, with `reason`, when the member cannot receive it (an erased account, no `conversation.receive`, the alert turned off). `conversationId` is the conversation of a message. Logged. Requires admin.announcements.

Ask the run under way to end before its next chunk, leaving what is sent as it is. Calling broadcasts.resume continues it. `runAt` names the run as broadcasts.status showed it: a conflict when the run under way is another one. Returns stopped false when none is under way. Requires admin.announcements.

With apply false it only counts the grants whose rule the member no longer meets (awards.revokeStatus reports it). With apply true it revokes them like awards.revoke: takes back the XP and the credits each gave (balances may go below zero), judging the member's other awards again with what is left until none more falls; members are not notified. Grants made by hand are never touched. A grant it revokes is granted again if the member later meets the rule. It runs in small chunks, only when called (never at deploy or from the sweep), and a run that stopped on an error resumes from where it stopped when called again with the same apply. Returns queued false when a run is under way. Requires admin.awards.

post.summary: Start a background run over every member that makes the site match the awards' rules at this moment: it sets each member's award XP, award count and per-award counters to what the grants they hold add up to (the level follows from the XP), takes back the automatic grants whose rule the member no longer meets (like awards.revokeUnqualified: their XP and credits are taken back, balances may go below zero) and grants the automatic awards the member meets and does not hold, with their XP and credits. Grants made by hand are never touched, and a grant revoked by hand is not given again. Members are not notified. With dryRun true it does all this chunk by chunk and undoes each chunk, so that awards.rebuildStatus reports what a real run would change (levels up and down, grants by award, credits, balances that would go negative) and nothing stays changed. A second run changes nothing unless rules depend on time, credits or XP, or credit rules pay for awards. It runs in small chunks, only when called; a run that stopped (on an error, or by awards.rebuildStop) resumes from where it stopped when called again with the same dryRun. post.summary: Create a shop item. Its rule, and a category's, may only use `cheap` criteria. A `frame`, `nameColor` or `threadCover` effect must name an entry of its catalog that has a picture or a colour. A `usernameChange` effect needs a consumable item (a validation error naming `isConsumable` otherwise), a `nameIcon` effect an item that is not (a validation error naming `isConsumable`). A consumable has no duration and cannot have a `group` effect. A `permission` effect must name a registered permission with a value of its kind; a `group` effect an existing group other than the guest group, ranked below the actor. Permissions of the admin category and groups that hold admin.permissions cannot be sold. Selling a permission or a group requires admin.permissions as well as admin.shop.

post.summary: Buy an active item of an active category, for yourself or, with `recipientId`, as a gift. An item the buyer cannot see because of its rule (or its category's) is not found. In one transaction: charges the buyer price x quantity (a conflict when the balance or the stock is short), adds the item to the recipient's inventory, lowers the stock and records the purchase. A consumable adds `quantity` units; any other item takes quantity 1 and is a conflict while the recipient holds it (after it expired it can be bought again). A permission or group item applies at once. An item that sells a yes/no permission of global scope the recipient already holds through something other than a shop item (a group or a staff role, for instance) is a conflict: there is nothing to buy. Number-valued and per-forum permissions, and a permission held only through another shop item, are always sellable. The recipient's inventory row records what the buyer paid. Requires shop.buy. A gift also requires shop.gift and a giftable item, and is refused when a block stands between the buyer and the recipient (whoever made it) or when their account was erased (conflict).

Move up to a better rank and pay the difference, less what the old rank is worth. The item must be an active `group` item; the member's current rank is the most expensive `group` item of the SAME category they hold: an active inventory row that has not run out (a rank past its end is not held, even before the expiry job marks it). With no current rank this is shop.buy at the full price. With one, the new rank's catalog price must exceed the old rank's catalog price (a conflict otherwise: ranks only go up). The credit is what the member paid for the old rank (not its catalog price today): in full for a permanent rank, and for a timed one the paid price times the share of its duration still ahead, rounded down. The member pays the new rank's catalog price minus the credit, never below zero. In one transaction the member is charged (a conflict when the balance is short), the old item leaves the inventory and its group with it, the new item is added and its group applies, and the purchase is recorded at the price paid. The new row is worth the credit plus the price paid, which is what a later upgrade credits. Requires shop.buy.

A consumable `permission` item is used without a thread. Every other item cannot be used: `frame`, `nameColor` and `nameIcon` are worn with appearance.set, `usernameChange` is spent by users.changeUsername, and `group` items and non-consumable `permission` items apply while held. An item past its end cannot be used, even before the expiry job has marked it. Requires shop.buy.

post.summary: Issue warning points. Requires member.warn over the member or, when it is about one of their posts (`postId`, which must be theirs and visible to the moderator), forum.warn over the member in that post's forum instead; the post is logged with the warning. The points, a type's or a custom value, may not exceed warning.maxPoints, and a moderator gives at most warning.perDay warnings in 24 hours (administrators have no limit by default). With a `typeId`, points, expiry and reason default to the type's (a locked type refuses a different `points` or any `expiresAt`); without one the warning is custom and needs `points` and a `reason`. `expiresAt` omitted takes the type's expiry, null never expires. post.summary: Delete a category or forum. Admins only (admin.nodes). `threads` says what happens to the threads in the node (and in the nodes deleted with it): `move` puts all of them, hidden or not, in another forum, which must not be one being deleted; `delete` removes them for good, with their posts, reactions, attachments, polls and the credits they paid. `children` says what happens to the nodes under it: `moveUp` (default) puts them under the deleted node's parent (each takes a copy of the deleted node's permission entries it has none of its own for, and an own view entry more open than what the same group or member had on the deleted node is lowered to that, so nothing becomes visible to anyone who could not see it; a member who saw it only through two layers that no longer meet gets an allow entry of their own; they go after the deleted node's siblings; a category that moves to the top level keeps the deleted one's tab; the forums of a top-level category cannot move up to the top level (a validation error, and the default `children` is `moveUp`, so say `delete` or move them first); `delete` deletes the whole subtree the same way. Nothing is refused for its size: the call only checks and queues a background job, which works through the threads in bounded chunks and removes the node when none is left. The forum the threads go to is judged again at every chunk: if it is gone or no longer a forum the job stops, the nodes stay read-only and the log gets `node.delete.failed`; calling again with an existing forum carries on, and so does a job that finds a forum under a top-level category at the end. While the deletion is queued nothing can be created or moved under the node (a conflict), and a forum another running deletion moves its threads into cannot be deleted (a conflict). Until then the nodes concerned are read-only and the job survives a restart. The call is logged as `node.delete` and the end as `node.delete.completed`, with the counts. A credit rule or reaction type limited to one of the forums, and a deletion already under way for the node, are conflicts. `actorPassword` is the acting administrator's own password, verified as for nodes.setModerator (a browser session must send it; an API key or token cannot delete a node).

A later post makes its thread unread again. Forums the viewer cannot see are skipped. Signed-in only.

A browser session (session cookie) must send it (missing: a validation error naming actorPassword). An API key or token cannot make this change: it is refused whether or not it sends a password.

The feed of conversations: threads and wall posts the viewer may open, newest first (`hot` is the exception, best first). Forums the site leaves out of the feed (`settings.update`, `feedExcludedForumIds`) and forums the viewer hides from their own (`feed.hideForum`) are not listed, with their subforums; naming a hidden forum in `forumIds` lists it again, a site-excluded one never. The filter fields (`forumIds`, `prefixId`, `type`, `tag`, `watched`, `unread`) narrow every scope, can be combined, and never widen what the viewer may open; with one on, only threads are listed, and a page can be short while `nextCursor` is set. `watched` and `unread` need an account. `latest` is everyone's activity, one entry per thread: the visible threads are walked by their last activity and each is listed once, with its newest visible post (its opening post, or its newest reply), merged with the wall posts by time. A reply moves its thread to the top; while paging, a thread that gets a reply is not listed a second time further down. A thread started by a member in a block with the viewer is left out, and one whose newest post is by such a member is listed at the newest post of anyone else. `following` is the activity of the members the viewer follows (the 100 followed most recently, when there are more) and requires an account: a thread is listed at the newest post one of them wrote in it, once per answer; a later page may list the same thread again, with an older post of a followed member. A cursor belongs to the scope and filter that issued it. `hot` is the threads that are busy right now among the forums the viewer can see, at most 50, each as its opening post, best first; it is recomputed every five minutes and not paginated (`nextCursor` is always null). A thread scores its replies, the reactions on its opening post and its views, divided by its age (a gravity formula), and is not listed before it has 3 replies or 3 reactions on its opening post. Threads hidden since the last refresh are left out and replaced by the next best, as far as the stored ranking reaches. Up to 10 featured threads (staff picks and paid promotions, see `threads.featured`) come first, newest feature first, whatever their activity, then the ranked threads without them, all within the same 50; they follow the same visibility rules. A featured thread beyond the 10 is listed only where it ranks. Threads of members in a block with the viewer are left out. A thread entry says whether the viewer may reply to it (`canReply`), why it is featured, if it is (`featured`; `latest` and `following` mark features too), and, for a signed-in viewer who has unread posts in it, how many and where the first is (`unread`, read from the viewer's read state for the whole page at once; none for a forum open for titles only).

The entries are those `feed.list` would put above `since` for this viewer, with the same filters (forums the viewer may open, wall posts they may see, blocks) and the same filter fields, counted through the same walks but never built: a thread that gets a reply counts again, as it moves to the top, and the viewer's own posts count too. A post approved after newer ones were posted keeps its old time and is not counted, nor is an entry made in the very millisecond of `since`. `count` is at most 99 and `more` is true when there are more than that. A hundred hidden entries in a row may make the count too low.

post.summary: Delete a thread for good: its posts, reactions, attachments, alerts, bookmarks, reports, watches, reads, bans, features and the credits it paid, and the thread itself. Only a soft-deleted thread can be deleted for good (a conflict otherwise), and one with a merge or split pending is refused. Requires forum.hardDelete in the thread's forum (administrators by default) and the right to see deleted threads there. An author with forum.hardDeleteOwn deletes their own thread in one step instead, without hiding it first, when it is not locked, holds only their own posts and fits one call. At most 500 posts go in one call, newest first and the opening post last: the thread stays (deleted) until a call returns `completed: true`, so a large thread takes several calls. Each call is one transaction and is logged as `thread.hardDelete` (`details.removedPosts`, `details.completed`, and the title and author, which stay in the log after the thread is gone). The merge tombstones that resolve to the thread go with it. Once a call has removed posts but not finished, the thread cannot be restored (a conflict). The member counters need no change, because a deleted thread no longer counts; the author's reaction score gives back the reactions the removed posts held.

Apply one change to up to 100 threads: move, lock, unlock, stick, unstick, delete (soft), restore, feature, unfeature, or set (or clear, with `prefixId: null`) the prefix. Every thread is judged on its own, with the permission of the single action in the thread's own forum (`forum.move` in both forums, `forum.lock` or `forum.lockOwn`, `forum.stick`, `forum.deleteAny` or `forum.deleteOwnThread`, `forum.undelete` or `forum.approve`, `forum.feature`; a prefix follows `threads.update`) and the same rules (a transfer pending, a thread that cannot be featured). The answer lists every thread in the order given: `changed` says whether it differed, `error` says why a thread was refused. A refused thread changes nothing; the others are applied, all in one transaction. Delete, restore and move cost in proportion to a thread's posts: once the posts (`replyCount + 1`) of the threads taken so far add up to 250,000, a further thread is refused with a conflict (`try again in a smaller batch`); the first thread is always taken. Each thread is logged in the moderator log as the single action is, with the shared reason, and its author is notified as for the single action unless `notify` is false. A thread listed twice is a validation error.

get.summary: One page of a thread's posts: positions [(page-1)*limit, page*limit), in position order. `cursor` (from the previous page) takes precedence over `page`. Posts the viewer may not see are left out, so a page can hold fewer than `limit` posts (moderators see every state; authors also see their own unapproved posts). `nextCursor` is null after the last page. `afterPosition` (the highest position the client holds) starts the page at the position after it, so a client can poll for replies: the answer is empty when there is nothing new. A `cursor` takes precedence over it, and it over `page`. With `afterPosition` the answer also carries `afterPostId`, the id of the post now at that position (null when there is none, or when the viewer may not see it, as with the items). Merging threads into this one renumbers positions, so the rule for a poller is: when `afterPostId` is not the id of the newest post it holds, drop what it holds and reload the thread from the start, ignoring the items of that answer; otherwise append the items. For a merge the check is exact: posts merged in below the held ones change the id at that position, while posts merged in above it and replies do not. A split does not renumber the posts that stay; it changes the id at that position only when the held newest post itself is split out, and a post that turns hidden for the viewer gives null. A poll does not show edits, removals or splits of other posts the client already holds, nor a post approved after newer ones were posted (it keeps its old position): those show on the next reload. While a merge into the thread is running, each answer costs a pass over the posts of the thread and its sources instead of an index read.

Requires member.viewIps over the member: refused for a member of equal or higher rank (a super admin is bound by none).

schema.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page.

network.description: The address itself for IPv4; the /64 for IPv6.

get.summary: The versions of the terms and the rules a member accepted, newest first (at most 50 of each page; the latest of each is always listed): kind, version, when, and the address recorded (null when none was recorded, when it was dropped at the log retention age, or when the reader lacks member.viewIps over the member), together with the versions the site publishes now (`current`, null for a page that is not published), so the reader sees what is missing. Read-only. Requires admin.members over the member.

The members who used an address, most recently active first, with how many times and when each was first and last seen there. An IPv6 address is matched by its /64 network (the network is returned, and a `/64` written out is accepted); an IPv4 address matches itself. Members of equal or higher rank than the caller are left out (a super admin sees all), so a page can hold fewer items than `limit` while `nextCursor` is set. A value that is not an address is a validation error. Requires member.viewIps.

schema.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page.

get.summary: The address a piece of content was made from, with the device and the member: `entry` is null when the log holds none (content from before the log, or made by an internal caller), when the content is not visible to the caller, or when its author ranks at or above the caller (a super admin is bound by neither; a guest ranks below everyone). A thread's address is its first post's. Private messages are not offered. Requires member.viewIps.

ip.description: Normalised: IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses appear as IPv4.

get.summary: The device, address and approximate place of each of the signed-in member's live sessions, by session id, parsed from the user agent the session was opened with, and when each was last used (to within a few minutes; null until a session opened by registration is first used). `terminalClient` names a device login (a terminal client's token, e.g. "sermo-cli · my-laptop", from the user agent the client sent); absent for a browser session. Only a browser session may ask.

The signed-in member's own recent sign-ins, newest first, successful and failed (a wrong password for this account), each with its time, device, approximate place and result. The log keeps rows for a limited time (see privacy.logRetention). Only a browser session may ask.

post.summary: The 'This wasn't me' link of a new-sign-in mail, without signing in: signs the member out everywhere (every session and API key). The signed token is the authorization; it works once, expires after a week, and stops working as soon as the member's sessions have been cut since the sign-in it was sent for.

get.summary: How long the site keeps the log of addresses, devices and places behind sign-ins and posts, in days. Public: the privacy and cookie pages state it.

The signed-in member's saved cookie choice, or null when they never saved one. The record may answer an older policy version than the site's current one (`site.get` `cookiePolicyVersion`): a client treats such a choice as none and asks again. Members only.

put.summary: Save the signed-in member's cookie choice on their account, replacing the previous one: the optional categories accepted (none to refuse all) and the policy version answered, stamped with `decidedAt`, the time the member made the choice (the banner's own record of it), else the time of the call; a `decidedAt` later than the call is replaced by the time of the call. The version must be the site's current one (`site.get` `cookiePolicyVersion`); a choice made under an older text is a conflict. Members only.

get.summary: Whether the cookie banner is to be shown to this visitor. Always true when the site shows it to everyone (the default), when the visitor's country is not known, or when it is in the EU, the EEA, the United Kingdom or Switzerland. The country comes only from the trusted location the proxy reports (see the location headers of the deployment); nothing the client sends counts. Open to everyone.

post.summary: Raise the cookie policy version by one, so every visitor and member is asked for their cookie choice again; saved choices of older versions stop counting. The version is changed only by this call, never by `settings.update`. Requires admin.settings.

get.summary: A member's saved cookie choice, for staff who must show it (null when none was saved, and for an erased member). Read only. Requires admin.members over the member.

post.summary: Sign a member out: one session by id, or all of them when `sessionId` is omitted. Signing out all of them takes effect on the member's next request, even with the session cookie cache on; one session by id also leaves the member's cached cookie valid until the cache expires (at most five minutes). Signing out all of them also revokes the member's API keys. Requires admin.members over the member, and also admin.permissions when the member holds any administration permission; a conflict for an erased member.

get.summary: The moderator log entries about one member, newest first: administrative edits, group changes, warnings, bans, restrictions and session revocations. Requires admin.members over the member: a member who ranks at or above the actor is not found (the actor's own log is).

schema.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page.

post.summary: Close a member's account for good and remove what identifies them. The account is marked erased and banned permanently first, in one step with its log entry (the ban cannot be lifted afterwards); then every session and API key is revoked and every pending reset or change-email link and queued account email is removed; their email is replaced by a unique placeholder and their password removed, so nobody can sign in or recover the account; their username becomes `Deleted member <id>` (with `-1`, `-2`, ... added if that name is somehow taken); their about text, title, signature, location, website, birthday, social handles, avatar and cover are removed and what they wear is taken off; their follows in both directions end; the address's delivery records (rejected addresses, failed sends), finished account emails, push devices and the profile picture of the login are removed; their referrer link, and the link of the members they referred, end (the referrer's count drops by one). What they wrote (threads, posts, wall posts, messages) stays as it is under the new name, and their ledger, warnings and log entries are kept. Not rewritten: `@name` mentions and quotation attributions inside other members' posts, which keep the old name. It cannot be undone. If a run stops part way, run it again: it finishes what is left and writes no second log entry. The actor's own password is required (five wrong answers in fifteen minutes from one session, twenty from all their sessions, block further attempts). Requires admin.members over the member, and also admin.permissions when the member holds any administration permission; refused for the last member holding admin.permissions; session actors only.

Who a batch would act on, without changing anything (a POST, because the selection is a body): up to 100 members matching the selection (a criteria selection looks at no more than 10,000 members in id order after `after`), each with their id and username (it lists the actor, super admins and members the actor may not act on too: the run skips them and says so), the names of a list that matched nobody in `unknown`, and `next`: the id to resume a criteria selection after, null when the members are all looked at or the selection is a list. `users.batchUpdate` acts on exactly these ids. A rule that holds a criterion too heavy to check while a request is served (the ones that count a member's history, which the promotions and awards run in the background) is refused, naming it. Erased accounts are never selected by criteria. Requires admin.members.

Apply one action to up to 100 members, named by the ids `users.batchPreview` returned (the rule or list is not read again, so the run acts on what was previewed): set the primary group, add or remove a secondary group, set or clear the custom title, remove the avatar, remove the signature, ban (for `days`, or for good with null; the ban obeys member.banMaxDays), lift every active ban, or erase the account (the erasure of `users.adminErase`). Each member goes through the permission and hierarchy rules of the single action and is one transaction (an erasure, several): a member the actor may not act on is skipped and reported, and the rest go on. Super admins and the actor are always skipped. Each member changed is one moderator log entry, as the single action writes it. Answers one outcome per member; an id that is no member is failed. An erasure that stopped part way is finished by running it again. Groups need admin.members and the actor's own password (session actors only, as `users.setGroups`); bans and lifting need member.ban; erasing needs admin.members, a reason and the actor's own password (session actors only). `reason` is logged with the change (the group actions log none) and, for a ban, sent to the member. Requires admin.members.

get.summary: The accounts waiting for approval, newest first, with what helps decide: username, email, when it signed up, whether the spam check flagged it, the country and (with member.viewIps) the address and the other accounts seen on it, and the terms it accepted. Only confirmed accounts are listed (an account that has not confirmed its email is not waiting for staff yet), and neither are the ones a ban holds back: a rejected one banned for good is closed, one banned for a time returns when the ban ends (an account whose erasure stopped part way stays listed, `erasureStopped`, so staff can finish it). The email is masked unless the viewer holds admin.members over the account. Requires member.approveRegistrations.

schema.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page.

post.summary: Approve or reject accounts that wait for approval, up to 50 at a time, one by one: an account that is no longer waiting, or that the actor may not act on, is skipped and reported, and does not stop the rest. Approving lets the account act as the member it is and emails it. Rejecting emails it the reason, if one was given, and either bans the account (`mode` `ban`, the default: the ban is the actor's own, so it needs member.ban over the account and is bounded by member.banMaxDays like `bans.create`: `banDays` null bans for good and needs -1, otherwise the days may not exceed the bound; a ban for good closes the account, a ban for a time keeps it held and out of the queue until the ban ends) or erases it (`mode` `delete`: the erasure of `users.adminErase`, so it needs admin.members over the account, as erasing a member does, and the actor's own password, session actors only; an erasure that stopped part way is finished by deciding again). Banning keeps the sign-up address and the terms record the queue shows for the next account; erasing removes them. Each account changed is one moderator log entry (`signup.approve`, `signup.reject`). Requires member.approveRegistrations over the account.

Close the signed-in member's own account for good: the same erasure as `users.adminErase` (read its summary for what is removed and what stays), logged as `member.erase` with the member as the actor and banned permanently like any erased account. The member's own password is required (five wrong answers in fifteen minutes from one session, twenty from all their sessions, block further attempts). It cannot be undone. Requires profile.deleteAccount; refused for a super admin (the flag is handed on first) and for the last member holding admin.permissions; session actors only, never an API key. Every session of the member ends, the current one included. If a step after the first fails, the account stays erased and banned and an administrator finishes it with `users.adminErase`.

Check the signed-in member's own password without changing anything; a wrong password is refused, and after five wrong answers in fifteen minutes from one session (twenty from all of the member's sessions) every answer is refused until the window moves on (a right answer does not clear the wrong ones). For clients that ask for the password again before a sensitive change. Session actors only (not API keys).

Ends the device login that sends this request: the Bearer token a terminal client got from `POST /api/auth/device/token`. The token stops working at once. The member's other device logins, browser sessions and API key stay. Only a device login may call it (`forbidden` for a browser session or an API key).

get.summary: The ban register, newest first: every ban with who gave it, why, when it ends and whether it was lifted. `state` narrows it to bans in force, bans that ran out, or bans lifted by hand; `userId` to one member. A page may be empty while `nextCursor` is set (the state filter is applied to the rows examined); continue until it is null. Requires member.ban.

schema.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page.

post.summary: A conversation message that is waiting for approval, with up to 3 messages before and after it, so a moderator can decide. The messages around it are only those a participant would see (visible ones); deleted and other moderated messages are left out. Requires conversation.moderate and that the message is in the approval queue. Every call is written to the moderator log (so it is a write); nothing else lets a non-participant read a conversation.

hideWhenLocked.description: What a member the rule excludes sees: false = the type greyed with a hint (`access` locked), true = the type left out of the picker (`access` hidden).

rule.description: Who may give the type, as a rule of cheap criteria (an empty rule is everyone). Criteria that measure the member's history (`measured` in criteria.list) are refused, so the rule costs at most three statements: the member's row, groups and purchases. Only for holders of admin.reactionTypes; null for everyone else.

access.description: What the viewer's standing against `rule` allows: `open` they may give it, `locked` they may not and the picker shows it greyed, `hidden` they may not and the picker leaves it out. A reaction already given with the type stays and counts whatever this says. The forum limit (`forumIds`) is separate and applies to the item.

lockHint.description: In the viewer's language, why a `locked` type is locked (the requirements, phrased from the rule's criteria; a plain "Locked" when the rule is too complex to phrase). Null unless `access` is locked.
